traits.label: Cap
traits.text: 8-25 cm in diameter. Convex to broadly convex, sometimes flat in older specimens. The surface is velvety to slightly sticky, deep brown to reddish-brown.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Cap: 8-25 cm in diameter. Convex to broadly convex, sometimes flat in older specimens. The surface is velvety to slightly sticky, deep brown to reddish-brown.

traits.label: Hymenium
traits.text: Tubular or poroid. Pores are initially small and red but become yellowish and larger with age, often staining blue when bruised.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium: Tubular or poroid. Pores are initially small and red but become yellowish and larger with age, often staining blue when bruised.

traits.label: Hymenium attachment
traits.text: Adnate to slightly descending on the stipe.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium attachment: Adnate to slightly descending on the stipe.

traits.label: Stipe
traits.text: Stout and cylindrical, often swollen or bulbous. Yellowish at the top, reddening downwards, and covered with a fine, mesh-like network (reticulate).
traits.raw: ℹ️ Stipe: Stout and cylindrical, often swollen or bulbous. Yellowish at the top, reddening downwards, and covered with a fine, mesh-like network (reticulate).

traits.label: Spore print
traits.text: Spore Print: Olive-brown to greenish-brown.
traits.raw: 🟤🟢 Spore Print: Olive-brown to greenish-brown.

traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Mycorrhizal, mainly associated with pine (Pinus) but can also be found with spruce (Picea) and other conifers.
traits.raw: 🌲 Mycorrhizal, mainly associated with pine (Pinus) but can also be found with spruce (Picea) and other conifers.

traits.label: Odour
traits.text: Not distinctive.
traits.raw: 👃 Not distinctive.

traits.label: Edibility
traits.text: Edible and considered very good.
traits.raw: 👑 Edible and considered very good.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: 8-25 cm tall.
traits.raw: 📏 8-25 cm tall.

traits.label: Microscopy
traits.text: Spores are fusiform, 13-17 x 4-5 µm.
traits.raw: 🔬 Spores are fusiform, 13-17 x 4-5 µm.

traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Closely related to the more famous Boletus edulis. However, its preference for coniferous forests, especially pine stands, and its redder coloration set it apart.
traits.raw: 🔤 Closely related to the more famous Boletus edulis. However, its preference for coniferous forests, especially pine stands, and its redder coloration set it apart.

ℹ️ Cap: 8-25 cm in diameter. Convex to broadly convex, sometimes flat in older specimens. The surface is velvety to slightly sticky, deep brown to reddish-brown.
ℹ️ Hymenium: Tubular or poroid. Pores are initially small and red but become yellowish and larger with age, often staining blue when bruised.
ℹ️ Hymenium attachment: Adnate to slightly descending on the stipe.
ℹ️ Stipe: Stout and cylindrical, often swollen or bulbous. Yellowish at the top, reddening downwards, and covered with a fine, mesh-like network (reticulate).
🟤🟢 Spore Print: Olive-brown to greenish-brown.
🌲 Mycorrhizal, mainly associated with pine (Pinus) but can also be found with spruce (Picea) and other conifers.
👃 Not distinctive.
👑 Edible and considered very good.
📏 8-25 cm tall.
🔬 Spores are fusiform, 13-17 x 4-5 µm.
🔤 Closely related to the more famous Boletus edulis. However, its preference for coniferous forests, especially pine stands, and its redder coloration set it apart.
